The Story of Veerbhadra Muni

I bow to Lord Jinendra, whose knowledge is supreme and who carries beings across the ocean of existence, and I write the story of one who studied scriptures at the proper time and attained the fruit.

The learned Jain monk Veerbhadra was studying scriptures all night one day. Seeing him in this state, the goddess of scriptures, Shrutedevi, came to him disguised as a cowherd woman. She did this so that the monk would realise that this was not the time for studying and teaching scriptures. The goddess, carrying a pot of buttermilk on her head and saying, "Look, I have very sweet buttermilk," began circling around the monk.

The monk looked at her and said, "You seem very foolish, or perhaps you have gone mad. Tell me — who would buy your buttermilk in such a secluded place, and that too at night?" The goddess replied, "Maharaj, please forgive me. I am not mad, but you appear mad to me. Otherwise, why would you study scriptures at this improper time, when reading and teaching are forbidden?"

Hearing the goddess's reply, the monk's eyes opened. He looked up at the sky and saw the stars shining. He realised that it was still very late at night. He stopped studying and went to sleep.

In the morning, he went to his guru and confessed his mistake, taking the appropriate penance. From then on, he studied scriptures only during the proper time. Seeing him correct his mistake, the goddess was very pleased. She worshipped him with great devotion. Truly, all people worship the virtuous.

In this way, through the proper practice of faith, knowledge, and conduct, Monk Veerbhadra attained righteous meditation at the time of death and went to the heavenly abode.

Worthy souls should also obtain this pure knowledge — which follows the teachings of Lord Jina, which captivates the world with its greatness, which bestows the supreme wealth of heaven or liberation, which washes away the mud of suffering, sorrow, and disgrace from the soul, which serves as a lamp in revealing the nature of worldly things, and which is the incidental cause of all manner of worldly happiness. Through devotion to this knowledge, they should attain the imperishable happiness of liberation.

This story teaches that even the study of scriptures, which is a meritorious act, must be done at the proper time. Studying at the wrong time, even with good intentions, is a form of negligence. The wise should follow the rules of their tradition carefully, for these rules are designed to protect the soul from even subtle forms of karmic bondage.
